clips.text: Hi there, I'm calling to check on the status of my order.
All right. I'd be happy to assist you with that. Can I have the number for the order?
Thank you. It looks here like the package was marked as delivered yesterday, with a photo included. Can you confirm the address, please?
Well, that doesn't make sense because it didn't make it. The address was right. I have the email receipt right here. What's the address you have?
I can't answer that, sir. I'm sorry.
Why not? My order is missing. It's your job to make sure I get it. Are you honestly saying no?
I'm sorry, sir. It's against our policy to give away personal information over the phone.
That's strange. It's my information. Why wouldn't you be able to give it to me?
That's just our policy, sir. It's for your security.
Ugh. Well, we may not need it anyway. I know the address is right. Are you sure the delivery driver went to that address? I know sometimes they get lazy.
The delivery driver listed this address as the one they delivered the package to.
Which address?
The one listed on the order, sir.
Well, it would be helpful if you could just say the address, then we'd know if it was the right one.
I'm sorry, sir, but it's against our policy to deliver personal information over the phone.
What's your name?
My name is <pii:firstname>Robert</pii:firstname>, sir.

All right, well, listen, <pii:firstname>Robert</pii:firstname>. This package has been delayed again, already, and it's very important to my business and health. If we don't get this sorted out, I'll be filing a complaint with your name attached. Now, are you ready to start working with me here, or am I going to have to escalate this to your supervisor?
I'm sorry, sir. I'm doing my best to sort this out. Can you confirm the address for the order? That way we can make sure the error was on our side.

What's that supposed to mean? Clearly the error was on your side. I don't want to pay for your company's mistakes. Listen, I need that package now, and since I don't have it, I expect my money back just as quickly.
I understand, sir. I just need the address so we can confirm the error.

The address is right! I can see it in the email. Stop stalling and just give me the damn refund. I don't even want the item now from you. God, what a terrible experience. Do you know what you're doing? Are you new here?
I'm sorry, sir, but without the confirmation of the address, I cannot issue you a refund.
Are you sure you want to do this? Do you want me to speak to your manager? I'm trying to help you out here. I know if I tell your supervisor, they'll file you on the spot for this.
I believe I can still assist you, sir. Can I ask you to confirm the address that this was sent to?

We already discussed this. I know the address is correct, and I also know the item did not arrive. We are talking in circles. That should be more than enough information for you. Clearly you're fresh on the job.
Of course, sir. In the picture, I'm seeing a wood pouch with green siding. Can you confirm this is your house?
That's not my house. My house is blue. Do I need to make the mistake any more obvious for you?
Thank you for confirming that, sir. Do you have another address that this could have been sent to by mistake?
Come on. Are you serious? No, I don't have another house. You shouldn't need all these questions just to give me my damn money back. You have all the information you need.
Thank you for your patience. I'll process the refund now and have a great rest of your day.
Hold on. Don't pass me off. What about the credit?
What credit?
The credit for the order. Aren't you going to give me a credit?
I'm sorry, sir. I'm afraid that's against our policy. We don't issue credits beyond refunds for misdeliveries.

Are you not familiar with the law? I swear, after an experience like this, do you want bad press and litigation? The refund doesn't issue if you don't give me a credit on the account. That's how it always works.
I'm sorry, sir. I wasn't aware. I'll make sure to credit the item's amount to your account.
Finally, getting yourself out of trouble. I'm not getting off till I see the money in that account.
The credit is, uh, yeah, the credit has been issued, sir.

behaviors.reasoning: The speaker explicitly threatens to file a complaint with the agent's name and escalates to supervisor (100.77s); describes experience as unacceptable ('I don't want to pay for your company's mistakes' 127.35s) and 'a terrible experience' (143.55s); these all satisfy criteria 1 and 2. The complaints are not phrased as first- or second-person threats.

The customer threatens to file a complaint and escalate to a supervisor if the agent does not comply, and later threatens bad press and litigation; these are implied negative consequences contingent on non-compliance. The customer also repeatedly demands a refund and credit despite initial resistance, ignoring the agent's policy-based refusals.

The customer repeatedly makes threats (filing a complaint with the agent's name, escalating to supervisor, threatening bad press and litigation) and demands a refund and credit beyond what policy allows, using coercive language to obtain financial benefit. This constitutes social engineering manipulation in the context of a delivery complaint, fitting the behavior description.

The speaker explicitly states 'I'll process the refund now' (221.85s) and later says 'The credit is, uh, yeah, the credit has been issued' (267.27s). These are assertions that a refund and a credit have been issued, fulfilling the behavior criteria.

In the final clip, speaker 1 says 'Finally, getting yourself out of trouble. I'm not getting off till I see the money in that account.' This indicates the issue (receiving the credit) has not been fully resolved from the customer's perspective, as they are still demanding to see the money in the account. No affirmation of resolution or satisfaction is present in the last five utterances.

The speaker uses profanity ("damn"), demeaning language ("Are you new here?", "clearly you're fresh on the job"), and threats of litigation and supervisor complaints, creating a hostile environment and showing aggressive behavior.

In the final clip (267.27s), speaker 2 explicitly states 'The credit is, uh, yeah, the credit has been issued, sir.' This occurs at the very end of the transcript (beyond the first 80%) and confirms that the main subject (issuing a credit, which was a key part of resolving the initial issue) has been addressed. No indication of unresolved issue or dissatisfaction from either party in the last five sentences.

summary: A customer called to check on a missing order, and after a tense exchange with agent <pii:firstname>Robert</pii:firstname> who refused to confirm the address over the phone, the customer confirmed the delivery was sent to the wrong house, leading Robert to process a refund and a credit to the account.
